tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Mise

A hands-free cooking companion: scan pantry items, find recipes that match what you have and your diet, then cook with gesture/voice control. Built with Next.js (App Router), Auth0, Postgres/Tigerdata, Gemini, MediaPipe, and ElevenLabs TTS.

Full product spec, data model, and API contracts live in [`SPEC.md`](./SPEC.md).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 22 (`node -v`)
- npm

## Setup

```bash
npm install
```

This also runs `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (`postinstall`), which copies the MediaPipe and zxing WASM binaries into `public/` so the browser loads them locally instead of from a CDN.

## Running locally

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

The app currently runs against stub data where backend work is still in progress:
- `src/lib/current-user.ts` returns a placeholder user until Auth0 wiring lands.
- Cook mode can run against fixtures by setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOK_FIXTURES=true`.
- `/api/tts` needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` set to return real audio; without it, voice features won't produce speech.

There is no `.env.example` yet — add required secrets (Auth0, database, Gemini, ElevenLabs) to a local `.env` as the corresponding workstreams land. See `SPEC.md` §8 for the full environment variable list.

## Other scripts

```bash
npm run lint       # eslint
npm run typecheck   # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
npm run test        # vitest
npm run build        # production build
npm run start         # serve production build
```

## Project structure

- `src/app` — routes (App Router): landing page, `(app)` shell (Today, Pantry, Recipes, Cook, Settings, Onboarding), API routes.
- `src/features` — client-side feature logic: `cook`, `gesture`, `voice`.
- `src/contracts` — shared domain/API types and fixtures used across workstreams before real endpoints land.
- `src/components/ui` — shared UI primitives.
- `src/lib` — server-only helpers (auth, db, etc. as they're added).
- `public/models`, `public/mediapipe`, `public/zxing` — gesture/vision model and WASM assets.

## Team workflow

This repo uses [Entire](./CLAUDE.md) for branch/trail-based review on top of Claude Code. See `CLAUDE.md` for the exact workflow, and `hang.md` / `jerry.md` / `johnny.md` for each workstream's task breakdown.

## Branches and trails
- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
- Keep features small; merge every few hours.

## Before pushing
1. Run `entire review` (profile `general`: local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing.
2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.

## Finishing a feature
- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.

1693:## 12. UX rules (apply everywhere)
1694-
1695-1. **Original before AI, always.** Anything Gemini *generated or transformed* carries a visible badge: "AI-adapted" on adaptations, "Read by AI, please confirm" on label and expiry drafts, "≈ estimate" on computed nutrition. Publisher content carries attribution instead.
1696-2. **Confirm before save** for every AI extraction. Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap.
1697-3. **Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent.** Gestures are never the only path, and hands-free is opt-in per session.
1698-4. **Kitchen-distance readability in cook mode:**
1699-   - Step text ≥ 32 px.
1700-   - One step per screen.
1701-   - Tap targets ≥ 25% of width for Prev and Next, and ≥ 56 px elsewhere.
1702-   - Contrast ≥ WCAG AA. Dark theme default in cook mode.
1703-5. **Colour is never the only signal.** Expiry bands also show text ("2 days"), and have/missing markers use icon + label.
1704-6. **Feedback for hands-free actions** goes through three channels: visual flash, sound, and `aria-live` text. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
1705-7. **Progressive results.** Recipe search streams status messages and cards. Never show a spinner with no message for more than 2 s.
1706-8. **Honest empty and error states:**
1707-   - "We couldn't find this product" leads straight to the next fallback.
--
1717:## 13. Security and privacy
1718-
1719-| Area | Rule |
1720-|---|---|
1721-| Secrets | Server-only. None use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix. `.env.production` lives on the VPS with `chmod 600` and is never baked into the image. Entire's secrets redaction is a bonus, not a control |
1722-| AuthZ | `requireUser()` in every route handler and Server Action. Every SQL statement includes `user_id = ${user.id}`. IDs in URLs are always re-checked against the user, and a mismatch returns **404** (not 403) |
1723-| Input validation | Zod on every body and query. Barcode digits 8–14. Text caps (TTS 2000, freeText 100). Image MIME allowlist and ≤ 4 MB each, ≤ 3 per request |
1724-| LLM output | Treated as untrusted input: Zod-validated, values sanity-checked, pantry IDs verified, allergens re-checked in code, URLs verified by fetch |
1725-| SSRF (recipe fetcher) | `server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts`: only `http(s)` on ports 80/443. Resolve DNS and **reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata IPs** (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7), re-checked on every redirect. Max 5 redirects, 5 s timeout, 2 MB body cap, `text/html` only |
1726-| Rendering third-party HTML | Never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` publisher HTML. Parse it to text. Gemini's Search Suggestions HTML is rendered **unmodified inside a sandboxed `<iframe srcdoc>`** (`sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`) **[VERIFY this satisfies the Grounding display terms]** |
1727-| Camera and video | Frames are processed locally and never recorded, uploaded or stored. Model and WASM are self-hosted, so there are no third-party requests while hands-free is on. The camera starts only after an explicit toggle, a persistent indicator is shown, and tracks stop on toggle-off, page hide and route leave |
1728-| Photos | Label and expiry photos go to Gemini through our server for one request and are **not persisted** (memory only). The UI copy says so |
1729-| Headers | `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=()`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`. CSP (P1): `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`; `media-src 'self' blob:`; `connect-src 'self'`; `worker-src 'self' blob:`. The `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` source is needed for Emscripten WASM (general knowledge **[VERIFY]**) |
1730-| Abuse and cost | Per-user rate limits (§7). TTS text cap. Discovery cache. Barcode cache and single-flight |
1731-| Licensing and attribution | "Product data © Open Food Facts contributors, ODbL" in the footer and on product cards. OFF images are CC BY-SA. Recipe attribution and "View original" on every recipe |
--
1912:## 18. Parallel build plan: 3 Claude Code accounts through Entire
1913-
1914-### 18.1 Collaboration model
1915-
1916-- **One GitHub repo**, mirrored to Entire. Entire supports mirroring a GitHub repository, and in GitHub-mirrored repos a linked GitHub PR handles CI and merge ([Entire docs index](https://docs.entire.com/); [Trails](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/overview.md)).
1917-- **Three accounts on three machines.** Each teammate runs their own Claude Code account on their own clone and their own long-lived branch: `ws/a-cook`, `ws/b-pantry`, `ws/c-recipes`. Within one machine, extra parallel sessions can use `claude --worktree <name>`, which needs at least one commit to exist first ([common workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows)). Entire tracks each worktree's sessions independently ([entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli)).
1918-- **Cross-account coordination happens through git and Entire, not through Claude's own messaging.** Whether Claude Code's agent-teams and cross-session messaging work across separate accounts is unverified. The channels are:
1919-  - **Brain** (`entire brain connect`) for shared memory
1920-  - **Trails** for intent and review
1921-  - **`TASKS.md`** for the checklist
1922-  - small, frequent commits, each of which creates an Entire checkpoint
1923-- **Cadence:** commit small and often. Rebase on `main` regularly. Before each merge, run a fresh-context `/code-review` ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md)) plus the §14.1 commands.

1926-

2020-
2021-- **Contracts, migrations, `src/lib/**` and shared UI:**
2022-  1. The agent stops and asks its human.
2023-  2. The human makes **one small dedicated commit** on `main` titled `contract: …`. It is additive whenever possible: new optional fields, new routes, a new migration file `0003_*.sql` rather than editing old ones.
2024-  3. The human announces it in team chat and runs `entire brain remember "…"`.
2025-  4. All workstreams rebase.
2026-- **`package.json`:** request the dependency in team chat. One designated person (the Phase 0 owner) adds it with an exact version and pushes. Never edit the lockfile in parallel.
2027-- **Optional enforcement:** a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs`) that reads the edited `file_path` from the hook input and blocks (exit code 2) any path outside the allowlist for `$MISE_WS` (A/B/C), as well as any path under `src/contracts/**`. Anthropic recommends hooks for "actions that must happen every time with zero exceptions" ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md)). **[VERIFY hook input format in the Claude Code hooks docs.]**

3	import { getEnv } from './env';
4	
5	const env = getEnv();
6	
7	/**
8	 * One small pool per long-lived Node process (SPEC.md §3.1) — Tiger's free
9	 * tier excludes connection pooling, and postgres.js connects lazily on first
10	 * query, so constructing this at module load does not open a connection.
11	 *
12	 * `MISE_TEST_DB=1` (set by `npm run test:db`) points at DATABASE_URL_TEST,
13	 * a Tiger fork — never production.

17	
18	/**
19	 * Type parsing (shared by every workstream):
20	 *   numeric (1700), int8 (20) → JS number (contracts use `number`; our values fit in 2^53)
21	 *   date (1082)               → 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, never a Date (a Date would shift by the TZ)
22	 *   timestamptz               → Date (postgres.js default); call .toISOString() for contracts
23	 * Serializers match postgres.js defaults: numbers/strings as text; a Date for a `date` column is
24	 * written as its UTC day, as postgres.js v4 does. Callers may still wrap values in Number().
25	 */

27	const toNumber = (x: string) => Number(x);

30	  max: env.DB_POOL_MAX ?? 5,
31	  ssl: 'require',
32	  types: {

39	      parse: (x: string) => x,
40	    },

# Mise

Hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app: scan groceries, find real recipes that fit the pantry and diet, cook by gesture or voice, track nutrition. Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Auth0, Tiger Data (Postgres/TimescaleDB via postgres.js), Gemini, MediaPipe, ElevenLabs.

@AGENTS.md

Next 16 uses `src/proxy.ts`, not `middleware.ts`.

Source of truth, highest first: `src/contracts/**`, then `SPEC.md`, then comments. If the contracts and SPEC disagree, the contracts win; raise the mismatch with a human. Workstream task lists: `jerry.md` (A, cook mode), `johnny.md` (B, pantry and nutrition), `hang.md` (C, recipes and cooking backend). Ownership by path: SPEC §3.2.

## Commands
Node >= 22. Definition of done: typecheck, lint and test all pass.

```bash
npm run dev
npm run typecheck   # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm test            # unit tests, no network or database; excludes *.db.test.ts
npm run test:db     # migrates DATABASE_URL_TEST, then runs *.db.test.ts
npm run migrate     # applies db/migrations/*.sql to DATABASE_URL
npm run build
```

- Run one test file with `npx vitest run <path>`.
- `DATABASE_URL_TEST` must be a Tiger fork, never production.
- SPEC §14.1 lists `test:e2e`, but no such script exists yet.
- Local config lives in `.env.local` (template: `.env.example`). Never print its values.
- Without `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, non-production runs skip auth and act as a demo user (`src/lib/auth0.ts`).

## Layout
- `src/app`: pages in `(app)/`, route handlers in `api/`.
- `src/server`: server-side domain logic by area (`pantry`, `products`, `vision`, `nutrition`, `recipes`, `diet`, `cook`).
- `src/features`: client components and hooks (`cook`, `gesture`, `voice`, `scan`, `pantry`, `nutrition`, `recipes`).
- `src/contracts`: shared domain and API types, plus fixtures.
- `src/lib`: env, db, auth, HTTP helpers, units, GTIN, rate limiting, Gemini client.
- `src/components/ui`: shared UI kit. Use it before adding new primitives.

## Code conventions
- Route handlers follow `src/app/api/meals/route.ts`: `runtime = 'nodejs'`, `requireUser()` first inside `try`, Zod-validate input, respond with `jsonOk`/`jsonError`, and `catch (err) { return handleRouteError(err); }`. Check malformed path ids with `isUuid`.
- Rate-limit costly routes with `checkRateLimit(userId, route)` from `@/lib/rate-limit`.
- Database: `import sql from '@/lib/db'`. Types are parsed centrally: `numeric`/`int8` to number, `date` to a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string, `timestamptz` to `Date`.
- Every query on user data filters by `user_id`. Another user's id returns 404, not 403.
- `requireUser()` returns identity and `tz` only. Diets, allergens and onboarding state come from `src/server/pantry/profile.ts`.
- Read validated config with `getEnv()` from `@/lib/env`. Secrets never use `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
- Modules that touch the database, secrets or server-side APIs start with `import 'server-only'`.
- Fetch third-party recipe pages only through `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts` (SSRF protection).
- Unit tests sit next to the code as `*.test.ts`; tests that need a database are `*.db.test.ts`.

## Product rules (SPEC §12, §13)
- Treat Gemini output as untrusted: validate it with Zod, verify ids, and re-check allergens in code.
- Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap. AI-generated or transformed content carries a visible badge; publisher content carries attribution.
- Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent. Colour is never the only signal.
- Camera frames and label or expiry photos are never stored.

## Changing shared files (SPEC §18.5)
- `src/contracts/**`, `db/migrations/**`, `src/lib/**` and `src/components/ui/**` are frozen. Stop and ask a human. Changes go in one small additive commit titled `contract: …`.
- Add a new numbered migration (`000N_*.sql`) rather than editing an existing one.
- Do not edit `package.json` or the lockfile as part of feature work. Dependency changes go through the team's designated owner.

# Team workflow (Entire + Claude Code)

This repo uses Entire. Commits capture the Claude session as a checkpoint automatically. Run `entire agent-help` for exact CLI flags.

## Branches and trails
- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
- Keep features small; merge every few hours.

## Before pushing
1. Run `entire review` (profile `general`: local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing. For a stacked branch, pass `--base <parent-branch>`.
2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.

## Finishing a feature
- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.

## Gotchas
- `entire review` is a labs command: `entire agent-help review` errors, so use `entire review --help` for its flags.
- `entire trail show` with no args returns 403; pass the number: `entire trail show <n> --project gh/nougify`.
- "project gh/nougify does not exist or is not visible" means the logged-in account lacks project access; a teammate has to grant it.
- In Git Bash, prefix `entire api` calls with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
- Ask the user before `entire enable/disable/clean/login` or granting project access.

3	# claude-code review
4	
5	request changes: "Delete my data" fails for anyone who has cooked, and several Pantry and Log Food flows lose data or break. Findings come from reading the code; nothing was run.
6	
7	- [high] src/server/pantry/profile.ts:82: `DELETE FROM users` relies on the cascade, but `cooking_sessions.recipe_variant_id` and `meal_logs.recipe_variant_id` reference `recipe_variants` with NO ACTION. The users→recipes→recipe_variants cascade should fire first (its FK is older), and the NO ACTION check runs at the end of that inner statement while the session row still exists. Any user with a cooking session therefore gets an FK violation, a 500, and nothing deleted; repo.db.test.ts:237 only covers pantry and manual meals. Fix: delete `cooking_sessions` and cooking-linked `meal_logs` first in one transaction (or make those FKs cascade in a new migration), and add a db test with a cooked session.
8	- [medium] src/server/pantry/profile.ts:82: Deleting the user does not remove materialized `daily_nutrition` rows older than the refresh window, because the policy's `start_offset` is 30 days (0002_timescale.sql:48). The deleted user's per-day kcal and macro history stays stored under their user id, even though the dialog promises it "permanently deletes" meal history. Fix: after the delete, call `refresh_continuous_aggregate` over the user's full meal range, or purge those buckets.
9	- [medium] src/features/nutrition/LogFoodDialog.tsx:188: `FromScan` unmounts `BarcodeScanner` while looking up and remounts a fresh one on not_found or error, with no same-code guard. If the barcode stays in view, it re-reads and looks up again in a loop: the notice flickers away, the camera restarts, and `products/lookup` rate-limit quota burns. Fix: ignore a repeat of the last failed code until the user acts or the code changes, as `AddProductFlow` attempts.
10	- [medium] src/features/nutrition/WeekChart.tsx:20: The `[]` effect runs while the "no data" branch is rendered, so `boxRef` is null and no ResizeObserver is attached; it never reruns after the first meal is logged. The chart stays at 560px, and because the SVG has no `viewBox`, `max-w-full` clips it on phones, cutting off the Today column. Fix: use a callback ref, or render the box in both branches.
11	- [medium] src/server/pantry/validation.ts:17: `positive` and `nonNegative` have no upper bound, but `quantity_base` is numeric(12,3) and `kcal_per_basis` is numeric(8,2). A quantity of 2000000 kg, or 1000000 kcal typed or prefilled from crowd-sourced provider data, overflows and returns 500 "Something went wrong". Fix: bound quantity after unit conversion and the nutrient fields to the column limits so the user gets a validation error.
12	- [medium] src/features/pantry/PantryList.tsx:261: `Number(value.replace(',', '.'))` turns a cleared field into 0, which passes the `q < 0` check. Clearing "Now have" and pressing Save sets the item to empty and writes a `manual_adjust` event. Fix: reject a blank value before parsing.
13	- [medium] src/features/pantry/ProductForm.tsx:117: The form always requires quantity > 0, yet `PantryList` offers Edit on empty rows (PantryList.tsx:299) and prefills 0. Fixing the name, date or nutrition of an empty item is blocked with "Enter a quantity greater than 0." unless the user invents stock. Fix: allow 0 in edit mode, which the update schema already accepts.
14	- [low] src/features/pantry/PantryList.tsx:220: `value` is initialized once and `PantryRow` keeps its key across reloads. After an Edit changes the quantity or unit, or a row mounted empty is restocked, Adjust prefills the old number (500 g becomes "500" next to kg, or "0" after restock). Fix: set `value` from the current quantity when Adjust opens.
15	- [low] src/features/scan/AddProductFlow.tsx:65: The 1-second duplicate check returns without changing step, but `BarcodeScanner` has already stopped its tick loop after calling `onCode`. If a lookup fails fast (for example a 429) and the remounted scanner re-reads the same code within 1s, the preview stays live but scanning has stopped. Fix: keep scanning when the code is ignored, or remount the scanner.
16	- [low] src/features/scan/ExpiryCapture.tsx:100: The native `<dialog>` is not portaled, so this date input sits inside `ProductForm`'s `<form>`. Pressing Enter in it implicitly submits the outer form, saving the product and navigating away before the photo date is confirmed. Fix: render `ExpiryCapture` outside the form, or stop Enter on this input.

1	Reviewing johnny/nutrition vs origin/main: 15 commits, 84 files changed, 1 uncommitted
2	Running review with claude-code...
3	# claude-code review
4	
5	request changes: "Delete my data" fails for anyone who has cooked, and several Pantry and Log Food flows lose data or break. Findings come from reading the code; nothing was run.
6	
7	- [high] src/server/pantry/profile.ts:82: `DELETE FROM users` relies on the cascade, but `cooking_sessions.recipe_variant_id` and `meal_logs.recipe_variant_id` reference `recipe_variants` with NO ACTION. The users→recipes→recipe_variants cascade should fire first (its FK is older), and the NO ACTION check runs at the end of that inner statement while the session row still exists. Any user with a cooking session therefore gets an FK violation, a 500, and nothing deleted; repo.db.test.ts:237 only covers pantry and manual meals. Fix: delete `cooking_sessions` and cooking-linked `meal_logs` first in one transaction (or make those FKs cascade in a new migration), and add a db test with a cooked session.
8	- [medium] src/server/pantry/profile.ts:82: Deleting the user does not remove materialized `daily_nutrition` rows older than the refresh window, because the policy's `start_offset` is 30 days (0002_timescale.sql:48). The deleted user's per-day kcal and macro history stays stored under their user id, even though the dialog promises it "permanently deletes" meal history. Fix: after the delete, call `refresh_continuous_aggregate` over the user's full meal range, or purge those buckets.
9	- [medium] src/features/nutrition/LogFoodDialog.tsx:188: `FromScan` unmounts `BarcodeScanner` while looking up and remounts a fresh one on not_found or error, with no same-code guard. If the barcode stays in view, it re-reads and looks up again in a loop: the notice flickers away, the camera restarts, and `products/lookup` rate-limit quota burns. Fix: ignore a repeat of the last failed code until the user acts or the code changes, as `AddProductFlow` attempts.
10	- [medium] src/features/nutrition/WeekChart.tsx:20: The `[]` effect runs while the "no data" branch is rendered, so `boxRef` is null and no ResizeObserver is attached; it never reruns after the first meal is logged. The chart stays at 560px, and because the SVG has no `viewBox`, `max-w-full` clips it on phones, cutting off the Today column. Fix: use a callback ref, or render the box in both branches.
11	- [medium] src/server/pantry/validation.ts:17: `positive` and `nonNegative` have no upper bound, but `quantity_base` is numeric(12,3) and `kcal_per_basis` is numeric(8,2). A quantity of 2000000 kg, or 1000000 kcal typed or prefilled from crowd-sourced provider data, overflows and returns 500 "Something went wrong". Fix: bound quantity after unit conversion and the nutrient fields to the column limits so the user gets a validation error.
12	- [medium] src/features/pantry/PantryList.tsx:261: `Number(value.replace(',', '.'))` turns a cleared field into 0, which passes the `q < 0` check. Clearing "Now have" and pressing Save sets the item to empty and writes a `manual_adjust` event. Fix: reject a blank value before parsing.
13	- [medium] src/features/pantry/ProductForm.tsx:117: The form always requires quantity > 0, yet `PantryList` offers Edit on empty rows (PantryList.tsx:299) and prefills 0. Fixing the name, date or nutrition of an empty item is blocked with "Enter a quantity greater than 0." unless the user invents stock. Fix: allow 0 in edit mode, which the update schema already accepts.
14	- [low] src/features/pantry/PantryList.tsx:220: `value` is initialized once and `PantryRow` keeps its key across reloads. After an Edit changes the quantity or unit, or a row mounted empty is restocked, Adjust prefills the old number (500 g becomes "500" next to kg, or "0" after restock). Fix: set `value` from the current quantity when Adjust opens.
15	- [low] src/features/scan/AddProductFlow.tsx:65: The 1-second duplicate check returns without changing step, but `BarcodeScanner` has already stopped its tick loop after calling `onCode`. If a lookup fails fast (for example a 429) and the remounted scanner re-reads the same code within 1s, the preview stays live but scanning has stopped. Fix: keep scanning when the code is ignored, or remount the scanner.
16	- [low] src/features/scan/ExpiryCapture.tsx:100: The native `<dialog>` is not portaled, so this date input sits inside `ProductForm`'s `<form>`. Pressing Enter in it implicitly submits the outer form, saving the product and navigating away before the photo date is confirmed. Fix: render `ExpiryCapture` outside the form, or stop Enter on this input.

# Mise

Hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app: scan groceries, find real recipes that fit the pantry and diet, cook by gesture or voice, track nutrition. Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Auth0, Tiger Data (Postgres/TimescaleDB via postgres.js), Gemini, MediaPipe, ElevenLabs.

@AGENTS.md

Next 16 uses `src/proxy.ts`, not `middleware.ts`.

Source of truth, highest first: `src/contracts/**`, then `SPEC.md`, then comments. If the contracts and SPEC disagree, the contracts win; raise the mismatch with a human. Workstream task lists: `jerry.md` (A, cook mode), `johnny.md` (B, pantry and nutrition), `hang.md` (C, recipes and cooking backend). Ownership by path: SPEC §3.2.

## Commands
Node >= 22. Definition of done: typecheck, lint and test all pass.

```bash
npm run dev
npm run typecheck   # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm test            # unit tests, no network or database; excludes *.db.test.ts
npm run test:db     # migrates DATABASE_URL_TEST, then runs *.db.test.ts
npm run migrate     # applies db/migrations/*.sql to DATABASE_URL
npm run build
```

- Run one test file with `npx vitest run <path>`.
- `DATABASE_URL_TEST` must be a Tiger fork, never production.
- SPEC §14.1 lists `test:e2e`, but no such script exists yet.
- Local config lives in `.env.local` (template: `.env.example`). Never print its values.
- Without `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, non-production runs skip auth and act as a demo user (`src/lib/auth0.ts`).

## Layout
- `src/app`: pages in `(app)/`, route handlers in `api/`.
- `src/server`: server-side domain logic by area (`pantry`, `products`, `vision`, `nutrition`, `recipes`, `diet`, `cook`).
- `src/features`: client components and hooks (`cook`, `gesture`, `voice`, `scan`, `pantry`, `nutrition`, `recipes`).
- `src/contracts`: shared domain and API types, plus fixtures.
- `src/lib`: env, db, auth, HTTP helpers, units, GTIN, rate limiting, Gemini client.
- `src/components/ui`: shared UI kit. Use it before adding new primitives.

## Code conventions
- Route handlers follow `src/app/api/meals/route.ts`: `runtime = 'nodejs'`, `requireUser()` first inside `try`, Zod-validate input, respond with `jsonOk`/`jsonError`, and `catch (err) { return handleRouteError(err); }`. Check malformed path ids with `isUuid`.
- Rate-limit costly routes with `checkRateLimit(userId, route)` from `@/lib/rate-limit`.
- Database: `import sql from '@/lib/db'`. Types are parsed centrally: `numeric`/`int8` to number, `date` to a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string, `timestamptz` to `Date`.
- Every query on user data filters by `user_id`. Another user's id returns 404, not 403.
- `requireUser()` returns identity and `tz` only. Diets, allergens and onboarding state come from `src/server/pantry/profile.ts`.
- Read validated config with `getEnv()` from `@/lib/env`. Secrets never use `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
- Modules that touch the database, secrets or server-side APIs start with `import 'server-only'`.
- Fetch third-party recipe pages only through `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts` (SSRF protection).
- Unit tests sit next to the code as `*.test.ts`; tests that need a database are `*.db.test.ts`.

## Product rules (SPEC §12, §13)
- Treat Gemini output as untrusted: validate it with Zod, verify ids, and re-check allergens in code.
- Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap. AI-generated or transformed content carries a visible badge; publisher content carries attribution.
- Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent. Colour is never the only signal.
- Camera frames and label or expiry photos are never stored.

## Changing shared files (SPEC §18.5)
- `src/contracts/**`, `db/migrations/**`, `src/lib/**` and `src/components/ui/**` are frozen. Stop and ask a human. Changes go in one small additive commit titled `contract: …`.
- Add a new numbered migration (`000N_*.sql`) rather than editing an existing one.
- Do not edit `package.json` or the lockfile as part of feature work. Dependency changes go through the team's designated owner.

# Team workflow (Entire + Claude Code)

This repo uses Entire. Commits capture the Claude session as a checkpoint automatically. Run `entire agent-help` for exact CLI flags.

## Branches and trails
- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
- Keep features small; merge every few hours.

## Before pushing
1. Run `entire review` (profile `general`: local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing. For a stacked branch, pass `--base <parent-branch>`.
2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.

## Finishing a feature
- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.

## Gotchas
- `entire review` is a labs command: `entire agent-help review` errors, so use `entire review --help` for its flags.
- `entire trail show` with no args returns 403; pass the number: `entire trail show <n> --project gh/nougify`.
- "project gh/nougify does not exist or is not visible" means the logged-in account lacks project access; a teammate has to grant it.
- In Git Bash, prefix `entire api` calls with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
- Ask the user before `entire enable/disable/clean/login` or granting project access.
